references.text: The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey was first given to Moses at the burning bush, where God promised to lead the Israelites out of Egypt into a good land.
The description of the Promised Land as a land flowing with milk and honey is repeated here in connection with the exodus from Egypt.
Israel is chosen and set apart from all other nations as a holy people for the Lord, reflecting the theme of God's election.
Israel's status as a holy people, separated from other nations, is confirmed here as the basis for God's laws.
The same chapter repeats the theme that God has set Israel apart from the peoples so that they may be holy to him.
Israel's calling to be a chosen people and a holy nation, distinct from other peoples, is established at Sinai.
The spies confirm that Canaan truly is a land flowing with milk and honey.
God's promise to Abraham to give the land of Canaan to his descendants as an eternal possession.
Peter applies the language of election and separation to the Christian church as a chosen people and a holy people.
Christ purifies for himself a people for his own possession, reflecting the theme of God's choosing of a special people.
